entries.expected_answer: The report says Viet Nam has upwards of 28 million children under 18, roughly one fourth of its 100.4 million population.
entries.evidence_quote: population of children under age 18 years in Viet Nam is upwards of 28 million, making up roughly one fourth of Viet Nam’s 100.4 million population.

entries.expected_answer: 8.4% of children under 16 remained multidimensionally poor in 2024.
entries.evidence_quote: By 2024, 8.4% of children under 16 years of age in Viet Nam remain multidimensionally poor

entries.expected_answer: Investments made especially during the first 1,000 days of life yield high returns. Examples listed include prenatal care, proper nutrition, immunisation, and early-childhood development and education.
entries.evidence_quote: timely investments in early childhood, especially in the first 1,000 days of life, yield high returns

entries.expected_answer: The cited evidence reports a 13% annual return on investment for high-quality early-childhood education programmes.
entries.evidence_quote: Compelling international evidence by Garcia, Heckman, and other authors, on the economic and societal returns of high-quality ECE programmes reveals a 13% annual return on investment (ROI)

entries.expected_answer: Upper-secondary completion was 74.8% for urban students and 46.4% for rural students.
entries.evidence_quote: Urban students (74.8%) are much more likely to complete upper secondary education, compared to rural students (46.4%).

entries.expected_answer: Suitable facilities and materials were available in 37.1% of primary schools, 28.9% of lower-secondary schools, and 19.9% of high schools.
entries.evidence_quote: Only a limited share of schools having suitable facilities and materials for students with disabilities, at respectively 37.1%, 28.9%, and 19.9% of schools at the primary, lower secondary, and high school levels.

entries.expected_answer: Overall, 45.4% of children received a minimum acceptable diet; the rate was 26.7% among the poorest households and 56.0% among the richest.
entries.evidence_quote: only 45.4% of children received a minimum acceptable diet, combining both dietary diversity and frequency. The richest households had the highest rate (56.0%), compared to just 26.7% among the poorest.

entries.expected_answer: Exclusive breastfeeding during the first six months increased from 19.6% in 2010 to 45.4% in 2020.
entries.evidence_quote: the rate of exclusive breastfeeding in the first six months markedly improved between 2010 and 2020, increasing from 19.6% to 45.4%

entries.expected_answer: Out-of-pocket payments account for half of total health expenditure.
entries.evidence_quote: out-of-pocket (OOP) payments, which currently account for half of total health expenditures.

entries.expected_answer: From 2018 to 2022, centralized drinking-water supply access increased from 86.7% to 94.2%.
entries.evidence_quote: From 2018 to 2022, Viet Nam made notable progress in access to adequate water and sanitation facilities. Access to drinking water through a centralized water supply system increased from 86.7% to 94.2% in the period mentioned.

entries.expected_answer: The share rose from 1% in 2015 to 1.4% in 2023.
entries.evidence_quote: Data from 2015 to 2023 show a modest increase in the proportion of children receiving child or family cash benefits in Viet Nam, from 1% to 1.4% (Figure 27).

entries.expected_answer: The report proposes initially expanding transfers to children under six and pregnant women, with a gradual move toward a universal child benefit for all children under 18.
entries.evidence_quote: Expand social protection and social assistance for children, introducing gradually universal(ist) cash transfers for children under six years and pregnant women (i.e., a universal child benefit), progressively until reaching the whole child population. The objective should be to gradually move toward a universal child benefit for all children under age 18

entries.expected_answer: 98.1% of children under five had a birth certificate nationally.
entries.evidence_quote: At the national level, 98.1% of children under five have a birth certificate.

entries.expected_answer: Endorsed in June 2021 for 2021-2025, the programme aimed to protect children's personal information and privacy online and support safe, healthy online interactions.
entries.evidence_quote: In June 2021, the first-ever National Programme on Online Protection and Support for Children’s Healthy and Creative Interactions 2021-2025 was endorsed, with the objective to protect children’s (personal) information and privacy when accessing the internet and participating in online activities and to support safe and healthy online interactions.
